title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning
layout_note: A bottom-up input stack (frames, encoders, feature grids, flatten) feeds one large module panel above it; the module's pseudocode sits beside it in its own panel, taking about half the width.
grouping: Left half, reading upward: three video frames on a time axis, a trapezoid vision encoder above each, a 3×3 grid of feature cells above each encoder with a time tag (t=0, t=1, t=2) added at a circled plus, a grey 'flatten' bar, a long row of small feature cells, and a large pale lavender panel (the module, titled in bold monospace with '× num_layers') containing a dashed box with a wide Attention bar, an FFW bar and residual circled-plus joins. Five pale lavender latent cells labelled 'Learned latent queries' enter from below at the right. A grey code panel fills the right half.
shapes_depth: Flat, square-cornered, borderless bars and cells. Visual features are saturated blue squares (grids per frame, then one flattened row), latent queries pale lavender squares; the vision encoders are blue trapezoids that narrow upward. Each feature cell sends its own thin blue arrow into the attention bar, while purple arrows carry the latents; five purple arrows leave the top. Inputs are tagged K=V=[X_f, X] and Q=[X] with X_f in blue and X in purple. Real photo thumbnails for the frames; monospace type throughout.
proposed_highlight: The module is the lavender panel with its name in bold monospace at the top-left; the learned latents are named in large purple text, the same purple as their arrows, the X tags and the output arrows.
lesson: Show resampling as a count: a long row of blue feature cells, one thin arrow each, enters the attention bar while only five purple latent cells come in and five purple arrows leave, so the compression to a fixed token number is visible without stating it.
notes: Layout: an input stack under a module panel, with a code panel beside it. Venue and year from the PDF footer (NeurIPS 2022).

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: A long row of flattened visual features (blue) and a short set of learned latent queries (purple) rise into one Attention bar (K=V=[X_f, X], Q=[X]); only a fixed small set of purple arrows leaves the top.

relations.form: a comb of ~25 thin blue arrows from the flattened X_f row and purple arrows from five latent cells (entering from below right) converge on one wide Attention bar
three video frames along a time axis at the bottom, each through an identical trapezoid Vision Encoder to a 3x3 blue feature grid with its own t=0/1/2 tag added
bottom to top: frames -> encoders -> grids + time embeddings -> flatten bar -> resampler panel (Attention -> FFW, each with a residual circled-plus) -> outputs
the attention/FFW pair sits in a dashed box marked 'x num_layers' rather than being unrolled
features drawn as cell grids per frame and as a long cell row after flattening, latents as a row of five cells, so the token-count reduction is visible as cell counts

channels.colour: stream identity: blue = visual features X_f (cells and arrows), purple/lavender = learned latents X (cells, arrows, labels) and the resampler panel itself
channels.shape: square cell = token, trapezoid = encoder, flat bar = operation, circled-plus = sum
channels.line: colour carries the stream (blue vs purple arrows); dashed rectangle = repeated block
channels.frame: lavender panel = the Perceiver Resampler; grey panel = pseudocode

quality.strengths: The method's point (many visual tokens in, few latent tokens out) is drawn as counts: a long blue cell row and a dense comb enter, five purple arrows leave; arrow colour follows the stream consistently and K/V/Q tags name what each attention input is; real video frames sit on an explicit time axis.
quality.weaknesses: The dense comb of thin blue arrows is visually noisy; the latent queries enter from the lower right and wrap round inside the panel with bends; the panel tint is the same lavender as the latents, so purple names both a stream and the module; the pseudocode panel takes almost half the width.

insights.structure: Left half stacks video frames, encoders, 3x3 feature grids with time tags, a flatten bar and a long feature row under a large lavender 'Perceiver Resampler x num_layers' panel; the right half is a grey pseudocode panel.
insights.data: Three real skateboard frames sit on a time axis at the bottom; features are blue cell grids, flattened X_f a long row of small blue cells, and the learned latent queries five lavender cells entering from below right.
insights.emphasis: Colour separates the two streams: blue arrows for visual features X_f, purple arrows for latents X, and both meet in the Attention bar labelled K=V=[X_f, X], Q=[X].
insights.flow: Bottom-to-top; many parallel thin blue arrows rise from the feature row into Attention, purple arrows from the latents, and a fixed small set of purple arrows exits the top.
insights.avoid: The dense comb of ~25 thin arrows from the flattened row is visual noise; a single bracketed arrow would say the same.

arrangement.units: module panel (lavender, with dashed inner layer box) above its input stack on the left; grey code panel on the right
arrangement.inputs_as: real video frames on a time axis
